subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that in △ABC, tan((B − C)/2) = ((b − c)/(b + c)) cot(A/2).

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Convert the sides to sines
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The 2R cancels from the top and the bottom, so the ratio of the sides equals the ratio of the sines.
steps.memory_tip: The 2R cancels top and bottom, so (b−c)/(b+c) = (sinB − sinC)/(sinB + sinC).
lines: By the sine rule, b = 2R sinB, c = 2R sinC

recall.must_convey: That the sine rule turns (b−c)/(b+c) into (sinB − sinC)/(sinB + sinC), and the sum-to-product forms give cot((B+C)/2) tan((B−C)/2).
accept: use the sine rule so b minus c over b plus c is sin B minus sin C over sin B plus sin C
the two R cancels from the top and the bottom
apply sum to product on both the difference and the sum of the sines
sine rule vaadithe two R cancel authundi, sum to product cheyyali
convert the sides into sines and then use sum to product
heard_as: cot of B plus C by two

steps.why: The result to be proved is written in half angles, so the sides must first become sines. The sum-to-product forms are the only step that produces half angles from B and C.
common_mistakes: Writing b = R sinB without the 2.
Using the sum formula for the difference of sines.

steps.label: Replace the half-angle sum
steps.margin_note: The other mark. The angle sum turns cot((B+C)/2) into tan(A/2), and dividing by tan(A/2) is multiplying by cot(A/2).

recall.must_convey: That (B+C)/2 = 90° − A/2 gives cot((B+C)/2) = tan(A/2), so tan((B−C)/2) = ((b−c)/(b+c)) cot(A/2).
accept: B plus C over two is ninety minus A over two so the cot becomes tan half A
use the angle sum to change the half angle of B plus C
divide by tan half A which is the same as multiplying by cot half A
ninety minus A by two kabatti cot ni tan half A ga marchali
the complement turns the cotangent into a tangent

steps.why: The angle sum of a triangle is what links the half angle of B + C to the half angle of A. Dividing by tan(A/2) is the same as multiplying by cot(A/2), which is the form asked for.
common_mistakes: Writing cot((B+C)/2) = cot(A/2) and losing the complement.
Leaving the answer divided by tan(A/2) instead of multiplied by cot(A/2).
